name: Asset Administration Shell (AAS) digital twin family (IDTA specifications and submodel templates)
scope_note: Covers the AAS as specified by IDTA (Release 26-01: IDTA-01001 v3.2, IDTA-01002 v3.2, IDTA-01003-a v3.1.1, IDTA-01003-b v3.0, IDTA-01004 v3.1, IDTA-01005 v3.2), the DPP-related submodel templates (IDTA 02099-1 DPP Metadata, IDTA 02035-1..7 Digital Battery Passport, IDTA 02023 Carbon Footprint and related entries on the content hub), the AAS-side DPP composition, discovery, history and signature mechanisms that IDTA added in v3.2, the ZVEI/IDTA DPP4.0 concept as context, open-source implementations and test tooling, and 2022-2026 literature. Left out: the content of IEC 63278 (all parts), IEC 61406, IEC 61360, ISO/IEC 29500 and every CEN/CLC/JTC 24 EN (bibliographic references only); the EN-side operation names, paths, clause and table numbers that the IDTA DPP annexes cite (rule 5 fence); dataspace connector mechanics (Catena-X, EDC) beyond naming them as a variant; OPC UA and MQTT AAS mappings; Part 3a and 3b content; live systems (none were contacted).
summary: In the AAS method a product passport is not a document type of its own; it is assembled from an Asset Administration Shell (AAS) that represents the product and from submodels that the AAS references. IDTA-01001 v3.2 defines the metamodel: an AAS carries AssetInformation with a globalAssetId and optional specificAssetIds, references to Submodels, and each Submodel holds typed SubmodelElements whose meaning is fixed by semanticId references. IDTA-01002 v3.2 defines technology-neutral operations, an HTTP/REST mapping with base64url-encoded identifiers in paths, serialization modifiers ($value, $metadata, $reference, $path, level, extent), cursor pagination, a JSON query language, and service specifications split into machine-identifiable profiles that a server lists at /description. The infrastructure services are AAS Repository, Submodel Repository, Concept Description Repository, AAS Registry, Submodel Registry, Discovery and AASX File Server. Version 3.2 (July 2026) added DPP-relevant features: AdministrativeInformation createdAt and updatedAt, an AssetKind value Batch, $history retrieval of the version valid at a date, $signed retrieval as a compact JWS, recent-changes queries, and an ID Link discovery pattern where the globalAssetId is a resolvable URL that returns an RFC 9264 linkset. IDTA 02099-1 defines the DppMetadata submodel (semanticId https://admin-shell.io/idta/cds/dppMetadata/1) whose Value-Only serialization is the passport header and whose contentSpecificationIds list names the semanticIds of the content submodels. An IDTA-01002 v3.2 annex describes the read path: resolve the product identifier through Discovery (or the ID Link), fetch the AAS directly or via a Registry descriptor, fetch every referenced submodel, select DppMetadata, select content submodels by semanticId, serialize them and merge them into one document keyed by semanticId. The battery passport is modelled by seven IDTA 02035 templates published in February 2026; their semanticIds mix https IRIs, an ECLASS IRDI and versioned SAMM URNs. Access control is specified in IDTA-01004 v3.1 as an attribute-based rule model over JWT claims with default deny, but popular open-source servers implement only role-based or no access control. IDTA's official test tool aas-test-engines (1.0.3, August 2025) checks files and read-profile APIs only against metamodel 3.0.1 and API 3.0.3, so the v3.2 DPP features currently have no reusable conformance suite. For a black-box engine the method is testable through HTTP responses, the /description profile list, the linkset, composed passport consistency, signed resources, access-control status codes and AASX or JSON sample artifacts.

maturity.adoption_evidence: Multiple maintained open-source servers and SDKs implement the AAS API (Eclipse BaSyx Java v2 milestone 15 of 2026-07-30, BaSyx Python SDK 2.2.0 of 2026-10-02, FA3ST Service 1.3.0, Eclipse AASX Server pre-releases to 2026-10-14, Eclipse AAS4J 2.0.2). Peer-reviewed prototypes of AAS-based passports exist for circular-economy, end-of-life, Gaia-X and battery use cases (see literature), and a 2025 survey-style comparison and a 2023 survey report that no open-source server implements the specification in all details. ZVEI published the DPP4.0 architecture proposal (2023) and IDTA promotes DPP4.0; a ZVEI showcase white paper reports 16 component manufacturers providing data via AAS (seen only as a search-engine abstract, secondary_only). Specification support in tools lags: most implementations declare metamodel 3.1.x, and the official test engine stops at 3.0.
maturity.regulatory_alignment: The method gives building blocks that map onto several essential requirements but leaves others to the operator. Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1) points (a)-(b) require a DPP connected through a physical data carrier to a persistent unique product identifier; the AAS links the product through AssetInformation/globalAssetId, and IDTA states that the DppMetadata uniqueProductIdentifier shall equal that globalAssetId, but IDTA does not fix the identifier syntax. Art. 10(1) point (d) asks for open standards and machine-readable, structured, searchable and transferable data; IDTA publishes the specifications and templates under CC-BY-4.0 with JSON Schema, XSD, RDF and SHACL artifacts and a query API. Art. 11 points (b) and (f) on access rights and update rights map to the IDTA-01004 access rule model, whose rights CREATE, READ, UPDATE, DELETE, EXECUTE, VIEW and ALL can be bound to JWT claims. Art. 11 point (g) and Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 78 point (g) on authentication, reliability and integrity map partly to the v3.2 $signed endpoints (JWS RS256) and to AASX package signatures. Art. 10(4) (backup copy through a DPP service provider), Art. 11 point (e) and Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 78 point (e) (availability after the operator ceases activity), and Art. 13(4) (upload to the EU registry) have no AAS mechanism; IDTA states that an AAS Registry is not the EU DPP registry and that no template exists for registration data. Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 77(2) sets three access groups for battery data and Art. 77(7) requires a new passport linked to the original after repurposing or remanufacturing; the AAS has no predefined construct for that passport-to-passport link. Law paraphrases rest on the 2026-10-13 repository record because EUR-Lex returned empty pages in this session.

L01_unique_identifiers.mechanism: Three identifier roles. (1) AAS id and Submodel id: Identifiable/id strings (IRIs, URNs or IRDIs); in HTTP paths they are UTF-8 bytes base64url-encoded without '=' padding, e.g. GET /shells/aHR0cHM6Ly9pZC5leGFtcGxlLmNvbS9teS1hc3NldC1pZA. (2) Asset identity: AssetInformation/globalAssetId (0..1, optional only for very early life-cycle phases) and AssetInformation/specificAssetIds (0..*, each {name, value, externalSubjectId?}); constraint AASd-116 reserves the name 'globalAssetId' (case-insensitive) for SpecificAssetId/name with the semantics of AssetInformation/globalAssetId. (3) Passport identity: IDTA 02099-1 DppMetadata properties digitalProductPassportId (xs:string, One) and uniqueProductIdentifier (xs:string, One); the IDTA-01002 v3.2 DPP annex states uniqueProductIdentifier shall correspond to the AAS globalAssetId, and the decomposition step maps it there. Operator and facility identifiers are plain xs:string properties economicOperatorId (One) and facilityId (ZeroToOne) without IDTA-defined syntax. Semantic identifiers (semanticId) are separate and use IRIs (https://admin-shell.io/idta/...), ECLASS IRDIs (e.g. 0173-1#01-AHF578#003) or SAMM URNs (urn:samm:io.admin-shell.idta.batterypass.product_condition:1.0.2#ProductCondition).

L02_data_carriers.mechanism: The AAS specifications define no data carrier. The carrier holds the identifier that leads to the AAS: in the IDTA ID Link pattern the carrier encodes the globalAssetId URL, which a phone camera can open; IDTA-01004 requires that access rules can be written for anonymous access so that such a scan works without a token. The ZVEI DPP4.0 proposal names 2D codes (QR or Data Matrix) and, alternatively, RFID or NFC carrying a manufacturer-domain URL. An AASX file or a compressed AAS serialization can itself be packed into a QR code for offline nameplates (research prototype, Otto et al. 2025).

L03_data_exchange_protocols.mechanism: HTTP/REST with JSON (application/json) as the profile serialization format; XML (application/xml) and AASX (application/aas+zip, changed in v3.2 from application/asset-administration-shell-package+xml) are available through GenerateSerializationByIds (GET /serialization with base64url ids and an Accept header) and the AASX File Server (/packages). ID Link resolution: GET <globalAssetId URL> with 'Accept: application/linkset+json, application/json;q=0.9' returns 200 with Content-Type application/linkset+json and a body {"linkset":[{"anchor":<ID Link>, "aas":[{href,type,profiles,authentication}], "aas-service-endpoints":[{href,type:'application/linkset+json'}], "dpp":[...], "dpp-service-endpoints":[...]}]}; links may carry profile identifiers per operation and authentication hints (type OIDC or OAuth2 with well_known_url, flows, scopes). Clients that ask for JSON directly may get 302 Found with Location to the AAS resource plus a Link header rel="alternate" type="application/linkset+json" (RFC 8288). Discovery lookup: POST /lookup/shellsByAssetLink (SearchAllAssetAdministrationShellIdsByAssetLink, body = list of AssetLink {name, value}, AND semantics, optional limit/cursor) returns AAS ids; legacy GET /lookup/shells?assetIds=<base64url(JSON SpecificAssetId)> is deprecated in v3.2. Registry: GET /shell-descriptors/{base64url aasId} returns an AssetAdministrationShellDescriptor with endpoints and submodelDescriptors; clients then call the endpoint href. Status mapping: 200, 201, 202, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 409, 500, 501, 502; error bodies are Result {messages:[{messageType: Undefined|Info|Warning|Error|Exception, text, code (1-32 chars), correlationId (1-128), timestamp (UTC pattern)}]}.

L04_apis_lifecycle_searchability.mechanism: Service specifications and profiles, each identified as https://admin-shell.io/aas/API/3/2/<Name>ServiceSpecification/SSP-<n> and listed by GET /description as ServiceDescription {profiles:[...], minItems 1}. v3.2 profiles: AAS Service SSP-001 Full, SSP-002 Read; Submodel Service SSP-001 Full, SSP-002 Read, SSP-003 Value; AASX File Server SSP-001 Full, SSP-002 Async; AAS Registry SSP-001 Full, SSP-002 Read, SSP-003 Bulk, SSP-004 Query, SSP-005 Minimal Read; Submodel Registry SSP-001 Full, SSP-002 Read, SSP-003 Bulk, SSP-004 Query; Discovery SSP-001 Full, SSP-002 Read; AAS Repository SSP-001 Full, SSP-002 Read, SSP-003 Query, SSP-004 Signature, SSP-005 Identifiable, SSP-006 History; Submodel Repository SSP-001 Full, SSP-002 Read, SSP-003 Template, SSP-004 Template Read, SSP-005 Query, SSP-006 Signature, SSP-007 History; Concept Description Repository SSP-001 Full, SSP-002 Query, SSP-003 Signature. Create: POST /shells, POST /submodels, POST /shells/{aasId}/submodel-refs, POST /lookup/shells/{aasId} (create-or-replace asset links), POST /shell-descriptors. Read: GET /shells, /shells/{aasId}, /submodels/{smId}, /submodels/{smId}/submodel-elements/{idShortPath} with idShortPath delimiters '.' and '[i]' URL-encoded; content suffix $value, $metadata, $reference, $path (no suffix = Normal); ?level=deep|core (default deep); ?extent=withBlobValue|withoutBlobValue (default withoutBlobValue); Content=Metadata with WithBLOBValue and Level=Deep with Content=Reference are not allowed; File content via .../attachment. Update: PUT /shells/{aasId}, PUT/PATCH /submodels/{smId} (PATCH with $value or $metadata). Delete: DELETE /shells/{aasId}, /submodels/{smId}, /lookup/shells/{aasId}. Search: ?assetIds=, ?idShort=, ?semanticId=<base64url>, POST /query/shells|submodels|concept-descriptions|shell-descriptors with the AAS Query Language JSON (field identifiers $aas#, $sm#, $sme#, $cd#, $aasdesc#, $smdesc#); recent changes: GET /shells/$recent-changes and /submodels/$recent-changes (experimental) and createdFrom/updatedFrom filters (date-time). Pagination: ?limit (integer, minimum 1) and ?cursor (opaque string); responses are PagedResult {paging_metadata:{cursor?}, result:[...]}; a missing cursor in the response means the end. DPP composition per the IDTA-01002 v3.2 annex: select the submodel with semanticId https://admin-shell.io/idta/cds/dppMetadata/1, serialize it Value-Only as the header, select the submodels whose semanticIds appear in contentSpecificationIds, serialize each and key it by its semanticId, merge; write path should be atomic with rollback.

L06_storage_archiving_persistence.mechanism: Storage is the operator's AAS and Submodel Repository (database or AASX-file backed, implementation specific). v3.2 adds history retrieval: GET /shells/{aasId}/$history?date=<date-time> (GetAssetAdministrationShellVersionByIdAndDate, AAS Repository SSP-006) and GET /submodels/{smId}/$history?date=<date-time>&level&extent (GetSubmodelVersionByIdAndDate, Submodel Repository SSP-007), returning the object valid at that time; GetAssetAdministrationShellById and GetSubmodelById also list a date parameter in the HTTP mapping. AdministrativeInformation createdAt (fixed at creation) and updatedAt (DateTimeUtc) must satisfy updatedAt >= createdAt and later versions have later updatedAt; IDTA says these are business values, so not every change must bump them. The IDTA-01002 DPP annex states that implementations shall keep an audit trail of all changes and select, per submodel, the latest version with updatedAt not after the requested date. AASX packages (application/aas+zip) give a portable archival copy. No IDTA mechanism for replication, backup to a third party or survivability.

L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.mechanism: IDTA-01004 v3.1 Access Rule Model (ABAC): access is granted only if at least one rule allows the action on the object, otherwise deny. Rule grammar (BNF and JSON Schema shared with the query language): ACL with ATTRIBUTES (CLAIM from the access token, GLOBAL such as time, REFERENCE to a value in the AAS), RIGHTS (CREATE, READ, UPDATE, DELETE, EXECUTE, VIEW, ALL), ACCESS (ALLOW or DISABLED); OBJECTS (ROUTE, IDENTIFIABLE, REFERABLE, FRAGMENT, DESCRIPTOR); FORMULA conditions; FILTER to strip sub-object data from READ results; reusable DEFATTRIBUTES/DEFACL/DEFFORMULA via USE*. The normative operation-to-RIGHT mapping for HTTP is an IDTA-01002 annex (e.g. PUT on a missing resource needs CREATE, on an existing one UPDATE; /invoke needs EXECUTE; GET .../attachment needs READ on the File element). Access tokens: signed JWT bearer tokens (RFC 7519) issued by trusted identity providers; required claims iss, exp, aud, sub, client_id, iat, jti; dataspace policy decides trusted issuers and attributes; anonymous rules are allowed for public passport data. Expected HTTP behaviour (informative conformance corpus): no credentials on a protected resource gives 401; deny gives 403 without payload leakage. ID Link linksets may advertise authentication (OIDC/OAuth2 well-known URLs). Implementations differ: BaSyx Java supports only RBAC with Keycloak-issued JWTs; FA3ST Service states it implements no security; AASX Server documents a rule language with FILTER blocks.

IDTA-01004 v3.1 says its mapping to the CEN integrity standard cannot be given yet. ZVEI DPP4.0 proposes X.509 certificates per actor for signing passport data.

end_to_end_flows.name: Consumer scan via ID Link and linkset (IDTA-01002 v3.2)
actors: ID Link landing service of the economic operator
steps: 1. Client decodes the carrier and obtains the ID Link URL, which is the AAS globalAssetId.
2. Client sends GET <ID Link> with Accept: application/linkset+json, application/json;q=0.9.

3. Landing service answers 200, Content-Type application/linkset+json, a linkset anchored at the ID Link with relations such as aas, aas-service-endpoints, dpp and dpp-service-endpoints, each link carrying href, type, supported profile operations and authentication hints.
4. A client that is not linkset-aware may instead receive 302 with Location to the AAS resource and a Link header rel=alternate type=application/linkset+json.
5. Client follows the 'aas' href, e.g. GET /aas/shells/<base64url(aasId)> with Accept: application/json, obtaining the AAS.
6. Client reads submodel references (ideally with referredSemanticId) and calls GET /aas/shells/<aasId>/submodels/<base64url(smId)> or $value for the relevant submodels.
7. Client composes the passport from DppMetadata and the content submodels, or follows the dpp relation to a pre-composed passport.

end_to_end_flows.name: Read passport by product identifier through Discovery and Registry (IDTA-01002 v3.2 annex, AAS side)
steps: 1. Client obtains a product identifier from the carrier.
2. POST /lookup/shellsByAssetLink with body [{"name":"globalAssetId","value":"<product id>"}] returns the ids of AASs whose asset information matches all pairs.
3. Client chooses an AAS id; several AASs may match.
4. GET /shell-descriptors/<base64url(aasId)> returns the descriptor with AAS endpoints or embedded submodel descriptors and endpoints.
5. Client calls each submodel endpoint (GET .../submodels/<id> or .../$value).
6. Client selects the submodel with semanticId https://admin-shell.io/idta/cds/dppMetadata/1 and serializes it Value-Only as the header.
7. Client selects submodels whose semanticId is listed in contentSpecificationIds, serializes each and places it under its semanticId key.
8. Client merges header and content sections into one passport document.

end_to_end_flows.name: Historical passport at a date
actors: AAS Repository with History profile SSP-006
Submodel Repository with History profile SSP-007
steps: 1. Client resolves the AAS id as in the flows above.
2. GET /shells/<aasId>/$history?date=2026-01-01T12:00:00Z returns the AAS valid at that time.
3. For each referenced submodel, GET /submodels/<smId>/$history?date=<same date> returns the version whose updatedAt is not later than the date.
4. Client composes the passport from those versions.

end_to_end_flows.name: Creation and publication by the economic operator
actors: economic operator or DPP service provider
steps: 1. POST /shells with an AAS whose assetInformation.globalAssetId is the product identifier and assetKind is Instance, Type or Batch.

2. POST /submodels for the DppMetadata submodel (uniqueProductIdentifier equal to globalAssetId, contentSpecificationIds listing the content semanticIds) and for each content submodel; add submodel references to the AAS.
3. POST /lookup/shells/<aasId> to create or replace asset links for discovery.
4. POST /shell-descriptors (or the operator's registry equivalent) with endpoints.
5. Optionally publish an ID Link landing service that returns a linkset.
6. Register the passport in the EU DPP registry by a separate, non-AAS call.

end_to_end_flows.name: File-based exchange and validation (AASX)
steps: 1. Supplier serializes the environment to aasx/data.json or aasx/data.xml (or *.aas.json/*.aas.xml).

2. Supplier writes /_rels/.rels with a relationship of type http://admin-shell.io/aasx/relationships/aasx-origin to aasx/aasx-origin (empty or 'Intentionally empty'), and aas-spec and aas-suppl relationships from the origin.
3. Supplier optionally signs the package with OPC digital signatures, then ships it as application/aas+zip.
4. Recipient checks package relationships, metamodel schema and constraints, then template conformance per submodel (e.g. aas_test_engines check_file).

end_to_end_flows.name: Signed retrieval
actors: Submodel Repository with Signature profile SSP-006
steps: 1. GET /submodels/<base64url(smId)>/$signed.
2. Server returns 200 text/plain with a compact JWS whose header has alg RS256, typ JWS, x5c, sigT and sid.
3. Client validates the x5c chain against a root certificate obtained out of band and verifies the RS256 signature.
4. Client compares the decoded payload with the Normal serialization of the same submodel.

failure_modes.fault: Server expects padded or standard base64 (with '+' or '/') identifiers, or raw percent-encoded IRIs, instead of unpadded base64url.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Probe the same resource with each encoding and compare status and returned id.

failure_modes.fault: DppMetadata.uniqueProductIdentifier differs from AssetInformation.globalAssetId (copy error or different identifier scheme).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Compare the two values after fetching the AAS and the DppMetadata $value.

failure_modes.fault: The QR code encodes a bare AAS id, its base64url form, or a URN instead of a resolvable URL, so a phone camera scan cannot reach the passport.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Decode the QR sample and check that the payload is an absolute http(s) URL equal to the globalAssetId or a specificAssetId value.

failure_modes.fault: ID Link endpoint returns the linkset as application/json, or with JavaScript-style comments copied from the IDTA example, or anchored at a different URL.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Check Content-Type, strict JSON parse and anchor equality.

failure_modes.fault: Only the deprecated GET /lookup/shells is implemented, so clients of Discovery SSP-002 using POST /lookup/shellsByAssetLink get 404 or 405.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Call both discovery operations and compare with the profiles listed at /description.

failure_modes.fault: Client and server disagree on the assetIds query parameter name (prose shows 'assetids', OpenAPI 'assetIds').
failure_modes.detectable_by: Send both spellings and observe whether filtering is applied.

failure_modes.fault: AASX downloads are labelled with the pre-3.2 media type application/asset-administration-shell-package+xml instead of application/aas+zip.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Inspect Content-Type of GET /packages/{id} or /serialization with an AASX Accept header.

failure_modes.fault: Registry descriptors point to endpoints that moved, so the client follows a stale href.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Resolve every descriptor endpoint and compare the returned id.

failure_modes.fault: /description claims profiles (e.g. History or Signature) whose operations are missing.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Exercise one operation per claimed profile.

failure_modes.fault: Pagination returns an empty-string cursor or loops on the same cursor.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Page through a fixture and detect repeated cursors or empty cursor values.

failure_modes.fault: $value wraps the value in a named object or omits empty lists, so the composed header differs from the template structure.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Compare $value with the Value-Only projection of the Normal response.

failure_modes.fault: contentSpecificationIds lists a semanticId with a different patch version than the deployed template (e.g. ...product_condition:1.0.0 vs :1.0.2), so a section silently drops from the composed passport.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Exact string match between contentSpecificationIds and submodel semanticIds; count of sections.

failure_modes.fault: Two content submodels share one semanticId (the battery PCF template 02035-3 reuses the generic 02023 Carbon Footprint id, and the battery Handover Documentation 02035-2 reuses the generic 02004 IRDI 0173-1#01-AHF578#003), so composition keys collide when an AAS carries both the generic and the battery variant.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Detect duplicate semanticIds among the AAS submodels and duplicate keys in the composed document.

failure_modes.fault: Template-derived instances keep idShort on SubmodelElementList children, as the 02099-1 1.0.1 artifact did for contentSpecificationId, which strict validators reject.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Metamodel constraint check on list children; diff against the 1.0.2 template.

failure_modes.fault: A v3.2 instance (createdAt, updatedAt, assetKind Batch) is rejected by a consumer or validator that implements metamodel 3.0 or 3.1.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Validate v3.2 samples with each pinned validator version and record disagreements.

failure_modes.fault: $history ignores the date parameter and always returns the current version.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Query a date before a controlled update and compare with the pre-update snapshot.

failure_modes.fault: Authorization is disabled by default (BaSyx feature flag) or absent (FA3ST), so restricted battery data is public.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Anonymous requests for restricted submodels; canary values in responses.

failure_modes.fault: Access rules filter GET /submodels/{id} but not /query/submodels, /serialization or AASX export.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Canary leakage probes on every channel for a low-privilege role.

failure_modes.fault: $signed returns application/json, omits sigT or x5c, or signs a payload that differs from the served Normal serialization.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Header inspection, JWS verification and payload comparison.

failure_modes.fault: The AAS Registry descriptor carries a globalAssetId or specificAssetIds that differ from the AssetInformation of the AAS it points to (descriptor not updated after a change).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Fetch the descriptor and the AAS from the descriptor endpoint and compare the identifier fields.

failure_modes.fault: The deployment accepts tokens, or presents x5c certificate chains, from an issuer that is not among the trust anchors the operator declared.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Compare the iss claim of accepted TEST-ONLY tokens and the x5c issuer of $signed responses with the trusted issuers and roots declared in the ICS; a token from an undeclared TEST-ONLY issuer must be refused.

failure_modes.fault: lastUpdate or updatedAt is not changed after content updates, so history and freshness rules give wrong answers.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Scripted update followed by comparison of timestamps.

failure_modes.fault: DELETE /shells/{id} removes a passport that must still be available.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Destructive probe on a disposable loopback fixture with a retention flag; otherwise manual review.
